2027-02-24.title: Wednesday of the third week of the Great Fast · The Finding of the Head of St John the Baptist
readings: Lot lingers, and the angels take him by the hand
There is no one who is righteous, not even one
The death of John the Baptist
2027-02-24.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), third week. Commemoration of the finding of the head of St John the Baptist.
2027-02-24.verse: But he lingered; so the men seized him and his wife and his two daughters by the hand, the Lord being merciful to him, and they brought him out and left him outside the city.
theo: The angels tell Lot to gather his family and leave Sodom, for the city will be destroyed. His sons-in-law think he is joking. At dawn the angels urge him again, “But he lingered.” Lot knows the danger and still cannot bring himself to go; his house, his goods and his habits hold him back. Then comes one of the most tender lines in Genesis: “the men seized him and his wife and his two daughters by the hand, the Lord being merciful to him, and they brought him out.” Even outside he bargains: not the hills, but a little town nearby, “is it not a little one?” And God grants it. In the third week of the Fast many of us are like Lot: we know what we must leave, and we linger. God does not abandon the one who lingers. He takes us by the hand. But he also says: “Flee for your life; do not look back.”

Paul's words are blunt: “There is no one who is righteous, not even one… All have turned aside.” Every mouth is silenced before God, “for through the law comes the knowledge of sin.” No one escapes Sodom by his own goodness; all of us need to be taken by the hand. Today the Church remembers the finding of the head of St John the Baptist, the prophet who called Israel to repentance. The Gospel tells how he died: John had told Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have her,” and for that truth he was imprisoned and beheaded at a banquet, to keep a foolish oath. St John Chrysostom contrasts the two men: John in chains was free, and Herod on his throne was a slave to his passions and to the opinion of his guests (in substance). Herod lingered between conscience and pride and chose pride. John did not linger; he spoke the truth and gave his life. His head, honoured by the Church through the centuries, reminds us that the voice which said “Repent” was not silenced.
outline: Ask: what are you still lingering over in this Fast?
Taken by the hand in mercy.
All need the mercy of God.
live: Name one sin or habit you know you must leave, and take one concrete step away from it today.
Where you have kept silent about something wrong out of fear, ask the Holy Spirit for courage and a gentle word.
2027-02-24.prayer: Merciful Lord, when Lot lingered in Sodom you took him by the hand and led him out. Take us by the hand when we hesitate to leave our sins. We confess that none of us is righteous before you; have mercy on us. Give us the courage of St John the Baptist, who spoke the truth to the powerful and gave his life for it, and keep us free from the pride that enslaved Herod. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Lamb whom John pointed out takes us by the hand at the altar and leads us out of every Sodom of sin.

quick: Lot lingered in Sodom, but the angels took him by the hand in God's mercy.
No one is righteous on his own; all need God's mercy.
John the Baptist spoke the truth to Herod and gave his life for it.
2027-02-24.action: Take one concrete step away from a sin you have been lingering over.
2027-02-24.question: What keeps me lingering when God says: flee?

family.explain: God sent angels to save Lot and his family from a bad city. Lot was slow and did not want to go. So the angels took them by the hand and led them out! God is patient with us when we are slow to leave what is wrong, and he takes our hand.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who finds it hard to change a bad habit.
family.ask: Ask: “What bad habit do we need God's help to leave behind?”

illus: A young man in Muvattupuzha had promised himself every Lent for five years that he would stop gambling on his phone. Every year he lingered: next week, after this match, after this bonus. This Lent his father, without a word of blame, sat with him one evening and helped him delete the apps, then gave him his old basic phone for the rest of the Fast. The son was angry for two days. On the third he said: I needed someone to take my hand. I could not walk out by myself.

pm.open: Merciful Lord, we linger. Take us by the hand and lead us out. Amen.
share: But he lingered (Genesis 19:16). Where do I linger?
There is no one who is righteous, not even one (Romans 3:10). Do I judge others as if I were righteous?
It is not lawful for you to have her (Matthew 14:4). Where does God ask me to speak the truth?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy and lead us out.
interc: For those caught in addictions who want to be free.
For prophets and truth-tellers in Church and society.
For journalists, judges and all who suffer for speaking the truth.
For those in power, that they may not be enslaved by pride.
For prisoners and those unjustly condemned.
pm.close: Father, you took Lot by the hand and gave John the Baptist the courage to die for the truth. Lead us out of our sins, free us from pride, and make us faithful witnesses to your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the angels urged Lot to leave Sodom. But he lingered; so the men seized him and his wife and his two daughters by the hand, the Lord being merciful to him, and they brought him out (Genesis 19:16).
We too linger over what we know we must leave. God is patient: he takes us by the hand. But he also says: flee for your life; do not look back (Genesis 19:17).
Paul reminds us that no one escapes by his own goodness: there is no one who is righteous, not even one (Romans 3:10). We all need the hand of mercy.

Today we remember the finding of the head of St John the Baptist. He told Herod: it is not lawful for you to have her (Matthew 14:4), and died for it. Herod lingered between conscience and pride and chose pride. John did not linger. Let us not linger either. Amen.
kids: Children, Lot was slow to leave the bad city, so the angels took his hand and led him out. God is kind and patient with us too. St John the Baptist was brave and always told the truth, even to the king. Ask Jesus to make you brave to tell the truth.

intro: Theme: “The Lord being merciful to him.”
On the day of the finding of John the Baptist's head: the man who lingered, the truth that all have sinned, and the prophet who did not linger.

sub: The sons-in-law thought it a joke.
Seized by the hand in mercy.
q: Seek the Lord while he may be found, call upon him while he is near;
See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!
points.apply: Make your Lenten confession this week instead of waiting for Holy Week.

q: They have all gone astray, they are all alike perverse; there is no one who does good, no, not one.
since all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; they are now justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
points.apply: Each time you are tempted to judge someone this week, pray: Lord, have mercy on us both.

sub: A foolish oath at a banquet.
q: Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Speak one necessary truth this week, gently and without fear.

concl: God's mercy takes the lingering by the hand.
John, who did not linger, was free even in chains.
2027-02-24.resolve: Leave behind, this week, the sin you have lingered over longest.
